findings.text: The fragment states the same-index raw MDAC channels magFlxLp28..34 'are mutually uncorrelated, so they are distinct signals rather than one duplicated'. Re-measured on the same common PSRC window, their mutual Pearson correlation is min|r| = 0.99991 (max 0.999999), i.e. near-perfectly correlated during this window, not uncorrelated; the manifest's evidence_inputs repeats it as 'min off-diagonal corr ~0'. The node's own dispersion measure flags PSRC magFluxLp28..34 as mutually uncorrelated (min|r| = 0.038), so the statement was apparently written about the processed channels but attributed to the raw ones. The identity/no-partner conclusion is unaffected, but the durable record carries a measurement claim inverted from the data.

The summary sentence says channels 28..34 'best residual exceeds 5 % of range under every candidate', but magFluxLp30's best residual is 4.96% (flux_loop_table.json row magFluxLp30, rel_residual 4.9595e-02), below the 5% threshold. The fragment's own flags section correctly omits magFluxLp30 from the high-residual list, so the prose contradicts the record's own output.

The fragment says, for channels 1..27, 'the two channels' ranges agree to within 0.3 %'. Re-measured, the raw ranges over the common window differ by up to 2.54% (magFluxLp3), and even the slope-scaled range a*ptp(MDAC) differs by up to 0.69%; the fitted slopes themselves span 0.985-1.030, a spread inconsistent with 0.3% range agreement.

justifications: Independent review of run r-20261006T043701845781-jtmm-flux-loop-correspondence (plan imas-ambix:jt60sa-machine-map section 5), reviewed_base_sha a9518f2d4f885b640c0eee7a3fb4636746357a66, reviewed_head_sha 54569fc36ee660ec447cc19aac6baaa2354b69bc, stored as a parsed record scoring all six dimensions in 0..20 -- goal_fidelity 19, evidence 14, scope_discipline 20, durability 12, fit 18, reuse 20 -- total 20 in the 0..120 sum. Goal fidelity is high: I re-ran the reviewed census script read-only against the cached E101154 store in a scratch copy and reproduced flux_loop_table.json byte-for-byte (identity_permutation false; nonunique magFluxLp28..34; high_residual magFluxLp28,29,31,32,33,34), confirming the identity correspondence for 1..27 and the absence of a unique raw partner for 28..34 without any geo.in assignment. Scope is full: the two commits touch only the single declared fragment HTML, the reviewed worktree is clean, no plan or product source is touched and no figure was written. Fit and reuse are strong: the fragment follows the sibling evidence-fragment idiom with element ids prefixed by the node id, and adds no code so nothing is forked or duplicated. Durability is weak: no test guards the correspondence, and the instrument (flux_loop_correspondence.py, instrument_check.py) lives only under the operator's run reports directory, outside version control, so a later reader cannot reproduce the numbers from the repository alone; the fragment's unsupported prose claims are themselves evidence that nothing checks them. Evidence is reduced below the required outputs because three quantitative claims in the fragment are false or unsupported against the cache: channels 28..34 do not all exceed 5% (magFluxLp30 is 4.96%), the raw MDAC 28..34 channels are near-perfectly correlated (min|r| 0.99991) not 'mutually uncorrelated', and the 1..27 raw ranges agree to within 2.54% not 0.3%. The required outputs (the 34-row table, the flag lists, the identity verdict, the positive control) are correct and reproduced; the errors are in the interpretive prose, one of which is recorded as blocking.
